Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.36.2 to 4.37.0
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.37.0

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

v4.36.3

No user facing changes.

Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956

4.37.0 - 08 Jul 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

4.36.3 - 01 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.2 - 04 Jun 2026

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.19.3 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 9 April 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.15, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3837
  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass
node scripts/check-plugin-sdk-subpath-exports.mjs: OK
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check: OK (baseline regenerated for the additive signature change)
pnpm tsgo:core: clean
git diff --check: clean
```





---

## Follow-up fix: mixed prose + parametrized invoke on the persist path

The initial scope covered zero-argument / self-closing invoke blocks. A separate, related leak was found afterward from a real captured session: a model turn that emits **leading visible prose** followed by a **fully-closed, parametrized** `invoke` block (namespaced or bare).

Root cause: `scrubOverCapPlainTextToolCallMessage` classifies such a turn as buffer state `"impossible"` (the leading prose means it is not a buffered tool-call prefix). When under the buffer cap it returned `undefined`, so the raw message was persisted and leaked to chat. The display path (`sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` → line-scanning `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) already strips this block, but the persist/normalize path did not, so the two diverged. Promotion cannot run for these blocks because a non-zero-offset block never parses as standalone.

Fix: before the `impossible` + under-cap `return undefined`, apply the same line-standalone `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` to each text block of the message content and return the scrubbed message, giving persist ↔ display parity. Behavior is byte-identical when nothing strips; tool execution is not widened (no auto-promotion).

Added mixed-content regression tests (bare and namespaced) asserting the persisted message carries no raw invoke XML, preserves prose up to the boundary, and does not auto-promote.
